detections.evidence_quote: They were either drowned in the lake itself, or they were tossed in the lake after they were already murdered.
detections.summary: Legend relayed that Native Americans were killed by settlers, drowned in the lake or thrown in after being murdered.

detections.evidence_quote: a ton of people have been murdered there
detections.summary: Some people attribute the road's name to many murders having happened there.

detections.evidence_quote: They'd slit your throat if you were traveling by, and steal everything that you were traveling with.
detections.summary: Highway robbers hiding under the trees would slit travelers' throats and rob them.

detections.evidence_quote: they hung them from all those low hanging trees
detections.summary: Locals reportedly caught the robbers, hanged them from the trees and left the bodies up as a warning.

detections.evidence_quote: another possible reason for the name of the road is actually a rather deadly malaria outbreak back in 1850.
detections.summary: A deadly 1850 malaria outbreak spread by mosquitoes in the local swampland, described by a doctor of the time, ended when the state drained the swamp in 1884.

detections.evidence_quote: this doctor, Doctor Doctor William Iro, commented back then on just how badly these people were affected by the malaria outbreak.
detections.summary: A contemporary doctor's written comment is quoted as the source for how severely residents were affected by malaria.

detections.evidence_quote: One man was robbed alongside the road, and he was actually killed with his own car jack
detections.summary: Three murders in the area are recounted: a man killed with his own car jack, a husband decapitated by his wife, and a man shot to death in an unsolved case.

verification_candidates.claim_text: New Jersey's draining of the swampy area in 1884 led to the malaria deaths there stopping for a while.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: they drained the swampy area, which luckily led to the deaths stopping for a while.
verification_candidates.rationale: Historical public-health causal claim that swamp drainage ended malaria deaths, checkable against records.
